tests/test_epg_match.py reads this file and never restates a number in
channelTotal 34 = 14 matched by the M4-01 strategies + 2 ambiguous on our
side + 1 ambiguous on the guide's side + 1 with no guide channel + 1 with
no tvg-id, plus the 15 F-EPG-11 address rows (7 matched, 8 refused).
The expected desc is 376 code points, not the 400 of EPG_MAX_DESC: the
cut falls at 400 in prose and redaction then removes the two URL paths.
That shortfall IS the proof that clean_detail redacted, in the data.
`sink` is the rule 5 case: the cut lands inside a URL's userinfo, so the
whole truncated token goes and the pad is all that is left. Its url and
forbidden list are vectors, not formatting, so a second implementation of
the same sink (Model.epgDetailText) can run them unchanged.
`addr` is F-EPG-11. Each entry carries the guide id the decision turns on,
so the test can read it out of the two fixture files and prove the join
was available before asserting what the matcher did with it.

note: On the frozen 1,453-channel list this strategy reaches 185 rows -- a
census of the STREAM url, the only field it reads -- 40 of them
reached by nothing else, and matched goes 226 -> 265. The round that
added it wrote 193 here, which is the stream-OR-LOGO union (stream
185, logo 64, union 193, logo-only 8). The URL LAYOUTS here are copied
from that list; the ids are synthetic.

Addr.us.why: the id is a path token of the row's stream URL and the guide name matches no row, so only the address can have matched it

AddrSlug.us.why: a guide id that is not hex: the strategy names no id shape

AddrTwo.us.why: one address names two guide channels; equal ranks are first-come and the second is contested, never merged

AddrRank.us@Web.why: ADDR over NAME: the guide's one declaration is offered to the Eastern row by name and to this row by its address, and the address names the playout

AddrFeed.us.why: ADDR over FEED: this id is also the feed base of feedbasetoken1@SD

AddrLogo.us.why: the id is in the artwork URL and not in the stream. Artwork provenance is not stream identity: 7 of the 8 real rows of this shape stream from a different distributor than the artwork

AddrShort.us.why: shorter than minToken, and a word 583 real addresses carry: the collision guard

AddrDupA.us.why: two rows stream this address, so it is ambiguous on our side and dropped rather than guessed

AddrDupB.us.why: the other half of the same ambiguity

AddrCase.us.why: the address spells it MixedCaseToken12. A URL path is case-sensitive, so folding case would read an identity the address does not assert

AddrRank.us@Eastern.why: matched this guide channel by NAME until the address reached the row that streams it; the brand is right and the playout is not

feedbasetoken1@SD.why: its FEED base is that id, and ADDR is asked first

AddrOther.us.why: it STREAMS the channel, but another row DECLARES it as its tvg-id and ID is consulted first

aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa0007.why: ID over ADDR: the row's own tvg-id is a declared guide id, which is a join the playlist author DECLARED, and it displaces the address claim that arrived first

why: The ID and ADDR maps both resolve this guide id, to DIFFERENT rows, so
the lookup ORDER decides it and the ranks do not: ID is consulted
first and the declaring row wins. UNVERIFIED on the frozen data -- 0 of
its 1,453 rows carry a tvg-id the guide declares -- so this is an
